passages.title: Greenhouse (original fiction)
passages.text:
The following text is from an original short story.
Marisol had expected the abandoned greenhouse to be empty, but it was ______ with life: ferns crowded every bench, and vines had climbed all the way to the cracked glass roof.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Foundations
passages.text: Bridges are usually admired for their spans, the distances between their supports. Engineer Tomás Reyes, however, argues that the most important part of a bridge is the part no one sees: its foundation. "A long span on a weak foundation," he says, "is simply a dramatic way to fail."
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Repair café
passages.text: Once a month, a community center in the town of Alder Creek hosts a "repair café," where volunteers fix residents' broken lamps, toasters, and bicycles for free. Organizers say the event keeps hundreds of items out of the landfill each year. Just as important, they add, residents who watch the repairs often learn to fix similar problems on their own.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Feeder survey
passages.text:
A student counted the birds visiting three feeders in her yard over four weeks. Each feeder held a different food.
Feeder | Food | Total visits
1 | Sunflower seeds | 212
2 | Thistle seeds | 87
3 | Suet | 145
The student concluded that, of the three foods, sunflower seeds attracted the most visits.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Canal town
passages.text: The town's first canal opened in ______ within ten years, the number of businesses along its route had tripled.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Letters
passages.text: The collection of letters, which spans four decades and includes notes from dozens of correspondents, ______ historians a rare view of daily life in the port city.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Coquí frogs
passages.text: Most frogs lay their eggs in water, where the young hatch as swimming tadpoles. The coquí frogs of Puerto Rico, ______ lay their eggs on land, and the young hatch as tiny, fully formed frogs.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Recycling notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Glass bottles and plastic bottles can both be recycled.
• Glass can be recycled again and again without losing quality.
• Most plastics can be recycled only a few times before the material degrades.
• Recycled glass is often used to make new bottles.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Tardigrades
passages.text: For years, many biologists assumed that tardigrades, tiny animals that can survive being almost completely dried out, protected themselves mainly by producing a sugar called trehalose, which helps shield cells in some other organisms. Yet when researchers measured trehalose in several tardigrade species, they found little or none. Further work identified proteins found only in tardigrades that form a glass-like gel as the animals dry, apparently protecting their cells until water returns.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Orchard poem
passages.text: In an original poem titled "The Old Orchard," the speaker describes a neglected orchard as both decaying and still productive, as this line shows: ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Exhibit
passages.text: The museum's new exhibit focuses on three everyday objects whose inventors are largely forgotten ______ the folding ladder, the safety pin, and the paper clip.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Volunteers
passages.text: Each of the volunteers who staffed the information booths ______ given a reusable water bottle at the end of the festival.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Two scientists
passages.text: Although the two ______ findings at first seemed to contradict each other, a closer look showed that they had measured the lake's temperature at different depths.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Park
passages.text: Some critics predicted that the redesigned riverside park would attract few visitors. ______ attendance during its first summer was double that of the previous year.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Mural notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Lin Adeyemi was a twentieth-century painter.
• She painted large murals in train stations.
• Her murals depicted ordinary commuters.
• Her 1962 mural Morning Platform is her best-known work.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Learning words (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
Some teachers argue that the fastest way for students to build vocabulary is to memorize lists of words and their definitions. Students can review dozens of words in a single sitting, and quiz scores often rise within days.

Text 2
Researchers who study reading point out that definitions memorized for a quiz are often forgotten within weeks. Words met repeatedly in meaningful reading, by contrast, tend to be retained, because readers see how the words are actually used.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Shell chains
passages.text: Marine biologists have observed that when an empty shell larger than any in a group appears, hermit crabs nearby often line up by size beside it. When the largest crab moves into the new shell, the next crab in line takes the shell it left behind, and so on down the line. This pattern suggests that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Historian
passages.text: Unlike earlier accounts of the mill town's decline, which blamed a single cause, the historian's new study is notably ______: she weighs several possible explanations and openly acknowledges the limits of the surviving records.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Highway lanes (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
Some transportation planners argue that adding lanes to a congested highway reduces traffic. As evidence, they point to a widening project after which average travel times on the highway fell during the following year.

Text 2
Researchers who study "induced demand" report that when lanes are added to congested highways, travel times often improve at first, but within a few years the new lanes tend to fill as more people choose to drive, and congestion returns to roughly its earlier level.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Library visits
passages.text:
A researcher compared library visits in three towns.
Town | Visits in 2019 | Visits in 2023
A | 12,000 | 15,000
B | 30,000 | 34,500
C | 8,000 | 10,400
The researcher noted that the town with the largest percentage increase in visits was not the town with the largest increase in the number of visits.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Shipwreck dividers
passages.text: Divers spent three seasons excavating a merchant ship that sank off the coast more than two thousand years ago. Among the hundreds of objects they recovered from the wreck ______ a set of bronze navigational dividers, still hinged, which suggests that the crew plotted courses on charts.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bridge repair
passages.text: Engineers inspecting the Larkin Street Bridge found corrosion in both its steel cables and its concrete anchorages. The city's repair committee had expected the cables to be the costliest part of the ______ anchorages, which had to be rebuilt underwater, cost nearly twice as much.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Botanical illustrator
passages.text: Trained as a botanist before she turned to illustration, ______ more than eight hundred plant species in watercolor during her expeditions, labeling each painting with the date and place it was made.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Pedestrian bridge cost
passages.text: The new pedestrian bridge uses about 30 percent less steel than the design it replaced. ______ it is expected to cost more to build, because each of its curved girders must be fabricated individually rather than cut from standard stock.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Songbird migration notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A researcher tracked two populations of a migratory songbird.
• One population nests in Norway; the other nests in Spain.
• Both populations spend the winter in West Africa.
• The Norwegian birds left West Africa an average of 9 days earlier than the Spanish birds.
• The Norwegian birds reached their nesting grounds an average of 11 days later than the Spanish birds.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Marsh grazing
passages.text: In one salt marsh, ecologists fenced snails out of some plots of cordgrass and left other plots open. After a season, the fenced plots held dense cordgrass, while many open plots had been grazed bare. In a nearby marsh where snail-eating crabs are abundant, however, the open plots looked nearly identical to the fenced ones. These results suggest that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Songbird pitch
passages.text: Ecologist Dara Mensah studies a songbird whose city populations sing at a higher pitch than its rural populations. Many researchers attribute the difference to traffic noise, which masks low-pitched sounds. Mensah instead hypothesizes that young birds simply learn the songs of the adults around them, and that the first birds to settle in the city happened to sing at a higher pitch.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Late quartets
passages.text: Composer Lena Ostrova's early string quartets were praised for their dense counterpoint, with all four instruments carrying independent melodies at once. Her later quartets abandon that density, often giving a single melody to one instrument while the others hold long, quiet chords. Some critics have called this change a decline in ambition. Ostrova's sketchbooks, however, show that she revised these sparse passages more times than any of her earlier music.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Committee report
passages.text: Although the committee's final report ran to more than two hundred pages, its recommendations were notably ______: each could be carried out within a single budget year by the city's existing staff.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Crater streaks
passages.text: For years, dark streaks that appear on the walls of certain Martian craters were widely thought to be traces of flowing salty water. When planetary scientist Teodor Lind compared the streaks' locations with maps of slope, however, he found that they occur only on slopes steep enough for dry sand and dust to slide on their own. Lind argues that the streaks are better explained as small avalanches of dry material.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Four-day week (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
Economist Rosa Iglesias argues that a four-day workweek raises productivity. She points to a group of firms where output per hour rose after employees switched to working four days a week.

Text 2
Labor researchers note that the firms volunteering for four-day-week trials tend to be ones whose managers already expect the change to succeed and whose work can easily be compressed into fewer days. Results from such firms, the researchers caution, may not hold for workplaces in general.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Seed germination
passages.text:
A researcher measured the percentage of seeds that germinated for two wildflower species at three soil temperatures.
Soil temperature | Species X | Species Y
10°C | 12% | 40%
18°C | 55% | 62%
26°C | 81% | 58%
The researcher claims that Species X's germination is more sensitive to soil temperature than Species Y's is.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Herd remains
passages.text: Archaeologists studying a 4,000-year-old village found that the sheep and goat bones in its earliest layers come almost entirely from young males; the females, by contrast, were usually kept into old age. Herders who raise animals mainly for meat tend to slaughter them young, whatever their sex, whereas herders who keep animals for milk tend to keep females into adulthood and cull most young males. The pattern in the village therefore suggests that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Festival lineup
passages.text: This year's festival lineup includes the Ramos Quartet, a string ensemble from Lisbon ______ Aiko Tanaka, a percussionist from Osaka; and the Northfield Choir, which will close the final evening.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Delta maps
passages.text: The hand-drawn maps that cartographer Ama Boateng produced during her survey of the river delta, many of which record channels that have since filled with silt, ______ now used by hydrologists modeling future floods.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Early reception
passages.text: When it was first published, the novel was dismissed by most critics as a minor work. ______ its first printing of two thousand copies took nearly a decade to sell out. Only after the author's death did readers begin to treat it as a classic.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Packaging notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mycelium is the root-like network of a fungus.
• Some companies grow mycelium around agricultural waste in molds to make packaging.
• Mycelium packaging is lightweight and absorbs shocks well.
• Unlike foam packaging, mycelium packaging breaks down in soil within a few weeks.
• Mycelium packaging currently costs more to produce than foam packaging does.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Covered market
passages.text: Many visitors to the old covered market in Varos assume that its maze of alleys grew without any plan. Historian Selin Aydın's study of property records complicates that view. The market's oldest section, she found, was laid out on a deliberate grid around two stone storehouses; only the later additions, built as trade expanded, wandered outward along whatever streets already existed.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Senator speech
passages.text: Observers who expected a conciliatory address were surprised: the senator's speech was ______ from start to finish, naming each of her opponents and listing what she saw as their failures one by one.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Drug trial in mice
passages.text: Though the drug's effects in mice were striking, the researchers were careful to ______ their findings, noting that the doses the mice received were far higher than any a human patient could safely be given.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Commute shares
passages.text:
A city opened a network of protected bike lanes in 2021. The table shows the percentage of the city's commuters using each mode of travel.
Mode | 2019 | 2023
Car | 70% | 62%
Bus | 20% | 20%
Bicycle | 4% | 12%
A city planner claims that the new bike lanes drew riders mainly from people who would otherwise have driven, not from people who would otherwise have taken the bus.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Island lizards
passages.text: Biologist Nadia Ferro introduced a ground-hunting predator to six small islands and left six similar islands untouched. Within a year, lizards on the predator islands spent far more time high in shrubs, and those with shorter legs, which grip narrow branches better, survived at higher rates than long-legged lizards. On the untouched islands, leg length had no measurable effect on survival. These results suggest that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Blue pigment
passages.text: The pigment—made by grinding a blue mineral that was carried by traders from distant mountains ______ was so costly that painters often reserved it for the robes of a painting's most important figures.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Glacier survey
passages.text: By the time the survey team finally reached the edge of the glacier, the storm ______ for three days, burying the markers the team had planted the previous season under nearly a meter of fresh snow.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Prototypes
passages.text: Neither of the two prototype drones performed as the engineers had hoped. Each lost power well before ______ battery was fully drained, a problem the team later traced to a faulty voltage regulator.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Chemist yield
passages.text: For months, chemist Lucia Ramos's experiments produced only trace amounts of the compound. ______ she noticed that the yield rose sharply whenever the reaction vessel sat near a sunny window, a clue that light was driving the reaction.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bridge notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Halden Bridge and the Morrow Bridge are suspension bridges.
• The Halden Bridge is 1,240 meters long.
• It was completed in 1931.
• The Morrow Bridge is 980 meters long.
• It was completed in 1937.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bee notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ecologist Mara Quist studied bumblebees in 40 city gardens.
• She counted bee visits to native and non-native flowers.
• Native flowers received about three times as many visits.
• Quist concluded that planting native flowers could help support urban bumblebee populations.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Cholera map
passages.text: In the 1850s, many physicians in London held that cholera spread through foul air. During an 1854 outbreak, physician John Snow mapped the homes of those who died and found that they clustered around a single public water pump. Workers at a nearby brewery, who drank the beer they were given rather than water from the pump, were largely spared. Snow's findings pointed to contaminated water, not air, as the source.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The letter
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story. Mrs. Hale has just received a letter.
She read the letter twice, the second time more slowly, as though the words might rearrange themselves into something kinder if given the opportunity. They did not. She folded it along its creases, laid it upon the mantel beside the clock, and turned to the window, where the afternoon was going about its business with a composure she could not help resenting.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: EV survey
passages.text: A survey asked drivers to name their greatest concern about electric vehicles. Among current owners of electric vehicles, 35% named the availability of charging stations; among drivers who had considered buying one but decided against it, 70% did. One might conclude that owning an electric vehicle eases worries about charging. But because the second group consists entirely of people who chose not to buy, the difference may instead reflect the fact that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Foundation soil
passages.text: Neither the architect nor the engineers ______ aware that the soil beneath the building site had been filled in decades earlier, a fact that came to light only when cracks appeared in the new foundation.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Transit hours
passages.text: The decision by the city's transit authority to extend service hours on weekends and holidays ______ riders who work late shifts, many of whom previously had to pay for taxis to get home.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Drought varieties
passages.text: Researchers expected that a drought-resistant wheat variety would outperform the standard variety most clearly in the driest years. ______ in the driest year of the five-year study, the two varieties produced nearly identical yields; the drought-resistant variety's advantage appeared only in years of moderate dryness.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Proof notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2022, mathematician Leah Okonjo proved the Harbor Conjecture.
• The conjecture concerns how many ways a network of points can be connected without forming loops.
• It had remained unsolved for 70 years.
• Okonjo's proof uses a technique from probability theory.
• Other mathematicians have since used her technique on related problems.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Printing press
passages.text: Many historians have argued that the printing press spread quickly across Europe because it dramatically lowered the cost of books. Historian Imre Halasz agrees that printing eventually made books cheaper, but he notes that in the first decades after its introduction, printed books often sold for about as much as manuscripts did. He also observes that the earliest presses clustered in cities that already had universities and established book trades.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Novelist themes
passages.text: The novelist's later work is far less ______ than her early fiction: where the early books announce their themes in the first chapter, the later ones withhold them until the final pages, if they disclose them at all.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Expedition water
passages.text: The expedition's success depended on a single resource ______ fresh water, which had to be carried in from a spring two days' walk away.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Recycling rates
passages.text:
City A began offering curbside composting in 2016; City B did not.
Year | City A recycling rate | City B recycling rate
2015 | 22% | 30%
2018 | 31% | 32%
2021 | 38% | 33%
Although City B had the higher recycling rate in 2015, ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Mathematical objects
passages.text: Philosopher Ana Ruiz contends that the long debate over whether mathematical objects truly exist has not been settled so much as ______: once the debate's key terms are clarified, she argues, the two sides turn out to be making compatible claims in different vocabularies.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Cat domestication
passages.text: Early accounts portrayed the domestication of cats as deliberate: people, it was said, tamed wild cats to protect stored grain from rodents. Genetic studies have complicated this picture. Domestic cats show far fewer genetic differences from their wild ancestors than domestic dogs do from theirs, and those differences arose gradually over thousands of years. Some researchers now argue that cats largely domesticated themselves, tolerating people in exchange for easy access to prey, long before humans took any deliberate role in their breeding.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Halted trial
passages.text: The trial of the new medication was halted ______ the results had looked promising, a safety concern emerged in the final month that the researchers could not explain.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Commute times
passages.text: City officials had hoped the new express lanes would sharply reduce commute times, but the effect proved modest. ______ the average weekday trip into downtown shortened by only about two minutes.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Opera notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Composer Inés Morales wrote the opera Salt Road (1998).
• Composer Daniel Oyelaran wrote the opera Harbor Lights (2004).
• Salt Road is set in a nineteenth-century mining town; Harbor Lights is set in a modern port city.
• Both composers built their operas from folk melodies they had collected from local singers.
• Salt Road is scored for full orchestra; Harbor Lights is scored for nine players.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Fertilizer and water
passages.text:
Researchers grew corn in plots that received different amounts of fertilizer and water.
Fertilizer | Yield with low water (bushels) | Yield with high water (bushels)
None | 20 | 30
Low | 21 | 38
High | 20 | 46
The researchers concluded that fertilizer increased yield only when water was plentiful.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Archive catalog
passages.text: Researchers hoping to use the archive's catalog to find letters on particular subjects have been frustrated: the catalog is ______, listing every letter's date and sender but saying nothing about what any letter contains.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bird counts
passages.text: Since the wetlands at the Maple Creek reserve were restored a decade ago, the number of bird species recorded there each spring ______ risen every year, according to volunteers who conduct the annual count.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Senator biography
passages.text: Critics had expected the biography to be a ______, given that its author had worked for the senator for twenty years. Instead, the book is unsparing in its account of the senator's failures, devoting entire chapters to decisions the author calls disastrous.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Night heat
passages.text: Most studies of urban heat have focused on daytime temperatures. Yet for human health, nighttime temperatures may matter more, because the body recovers from daytime heat stress only when temperatures fall after dark. Climatologist Kofi Asante's measurements show that in dense neighborhoods, pavement and buildings release stored heat at night, keeping nights as much as 5°C warmer than in nearby parks.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Salmon decline
passages.text: For decades, the decline of salmon in the Varna River was blamed on overfishing. When fishing limits were tightened in the 1990s, however, salmon numbers kept falling. Biologist Mara Lindqvist then noticed that the decline closely tracked the construction of small dams on the river's tributaries, which block salmon from reaching their spawning streams. Since several of those dams were removed in 2015, salmon counts in the affected tributaries have tripled.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Nesting success
passages.text:
Researchers recorded the percentage of nests that produced at least one fledgling for two bird species at a wetland preserve.
Year | Species A | Species B
2015 | 70% | 40%
2018 | 66% | 52%
2021 | 63% | 60%
The researchers noted that the gap between the two species' nesting success narrowed considerably over this period.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Cotton pests
passages.text: In laboratory trials, a pest-resistant cotton strain reduced caterpillar damage by 90 percent, but in farm trials the reduction was only 40 percent. The researchers found that on farms, caterpillars often fed first on weeds growing between the rows of cotton, which let them grow larger before moving onto the cotton plants, and larger caterpillars are much less affected by the strain's toxin. These findings suggest that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Poet phrase
passages.text: In a 1962 interview, the poet described her hometown as ______ a phrase that later became the title of her best-known collection.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Sample collection
passages.text: Having spent three years collecting soil samples from more than two hundred farms, ______ for the care with which she documented each site.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bus routes
passages.text: The committee's report found no evidence that the new bus routes had reduced overall ridership. ______ it recommended that the city restore two of the old routes, citing complaints from riders who now faced much longer walks to their stops.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Tide gauge notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A tide gauge records the height of the sea surface at one location.
• Readings are usually taken every few minutes.
• Long records from tide gauges help scientists track changes in average sea level.
• The gauge at Port Ellery has operated continuously since 1904.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Base rates
passages.text: In a survey of people who had developed a certain digestive condition, 80% reported regularly drinking a popular brand of sparkling water. A commentator cited this figure as evidence that the drink may cause the condition. But in the population as a whole, about 80% of people also report regularly drinking that brand, which suggests that ______
passages.author: ai:claude
